title: Non-Equilibrium Instantaneous Approximation and Dipole Forbidden d-d Transitions
authors: Marco Marino, Lasse Sternemann, Mirko Cinchetti, Frithjof B. Anders
abstract: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy provides direct access to pump-induced changes in the electronic structure of correlated materials, but its theoretical description generally requires computationally demanding two-time non-equilibrium calculations. We introduce an instantaneous approximation for pump-driven correlated systems, based on a separation between the rapid decay of the Green's functions in the relative time variable and their slower evolution in the average time. Combined with a one-shot dynamical mean-field construction at the Hubbard I level, the method incorporates the driven dynamics of the local correlated shell into the lattice Green's function while retaining momentum resolution. We also derive an effective coupling for nominally dipole-forbidden d-d excitations. It arises from a dipole-allowed d-p transition followed by p-d hybridization; beyond the instantaneous limit, the same process produces an energy-dependent vertex correction to the optical response. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to paramagnetic and antiferromagnetic FePS3, using a density-functional theory derived tight-binding model together with a supercell unfolding procedure. The calculated momentum-resolved spectra reproduce the main qualitative features observed after excitation of the first and second d-d transitions in recent time-resolved photoemission experiments.
summary: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on correlated materials by introducing an Instantaneous Approximation combined with a one-shot Hubbard I approach. This method successfully incorporates local electronic correlations while retaining momentum resolution. The framework is validated using $	ext{FePS}_3$, demonstrating its ability to reproduce key features of experimentally observed d-d excitations.
main_problem: The theoretical description of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (trARPES) on correlated materials following optical excitation is computationally demanding.
main_result: The proposed Non-Equilibrium Instantaneous Approximation successfully reproduces the main qualitative features observed in experimental momentum-resolved spectra for d-d excitations in $	ext{FePS}_3$.
method: The authors introduce an instantaneous approximation (IAP) combined with a one-shot Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) construction at the Hubbard I level to handle non-equilibrium dynamics.
model_or_system: The study focuses on correlated materials like $	ext{FePS}_3$, modeled using DFT derived tight-binding Hamiltonians incorporating local Coulomb interactions. The formalism is built upon the Keldysh-Kadanoff-Baym (KB) equations.
key_observables: Momentum-resolved electronic structure, spectral function $ho(\omega, \vec{k})$, and signatures of first and second d-d excitations.
important_parameters: The approximation is valid when electron dynamics are much faster than the pulse duration ($	au_p > 100 	ext{fs}$); the Hubbard I approach is used to treat local correlations.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the Instantaneous Approximation (IAP), which separates time scales, allowing for a one-shot calculation instead of full non-equilibrium self-consistency.
figures_summary: Figures compare calculated K-maps and band structures from DFT + Hubbard I + $\Lambda$ using both standard methods and the proposed IAP approximation against experimental ARPES data for paramagnetic $	ext{FePS}_3$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the NEQ-IAP framework, applies it to the correlated system ($	ext{FePS}_3$), derives an effective coupling for forbidden transitions, and validates the method by comparing calculated momentum-resolved spectra against existing time-resolved photoemission experiments.
why_interesting: This work provides a computationally tractable yet physically rigorous theoretical tool (IAP + DMFT) to model ultrafast dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which is crucial for understanding light-matter interaction in quantum materials.
